sources.title: Dene Nation home
sources.note: Community authority identifying Denendeh as the Land of the People and representing living Dene communities.

sources.title: Dene Nation: Our Nation
sources.note: Community account of Denendeh, five distinct regional groups, languages, territories, oral history, and stewardship.

sources.title: Dene Nation Lands, Water and Environment
sources.note: Community authority on water, land, wildlife, consent, knowledge protocols, and relationships across Denendeh.

sources.title: Dene Nation Constitution Reform Commission
sources.note: Community account of distinct governing structures, story-based law, values, consultation, and collective decision making.

sources.title: Dene Nation Constitution
sources.note: Dene Nation constitutional statement recognizing distinct territories, governments, oral treaties, and responsibilities.

sources.title: Dene Knowledge Protocol Guide
sources.note: Community protocol on knowledge diversity, consent, ownership, context, and respectful use rather than extraction.

sources.title: Denendeh Development Corporation: About Us
sources.note: Dene-owned institution explaining the modern political and geographic use of Denendeh across five regions.

sources.title: Government of Northwest Territories: Dene Kede
sources.note: Elder-informed curriculum framing lifelong learning through land, people, self, spirituality, language, and capable citizenship.

sources.title: Dene Kede K to 6 curriculum
sources.note: Detailed community-developed curriculum connecting children, observation, guided practice, stories, land skills, and relationships.

sources.title: Dene Kede teacher resource manual
sources.note: Teacher resource describing traditional Dene education through family, Elders, experience, practice, and community participation.

sources.title: Our Languages curriculum
sources.note: Territorial curriculum distinguishing Dene languages, communities, dialects, oral proficiency, and language learning.

sources.title: Official Indigenous languages and dialects spoken by community
sources.note: Government community-by-community reference showing that several distinct Dene languages and dialects are spoken.

sources.title: Indigenous Languages Alphabets
sources.note: Modern official alphabets for several distinct NWT Dene languages, including tone, nasality, and specialized letters.

sources.title: SSHRC: Word associations
sources.note: Research partnership describing primarily oral Dene language documentation and later community work on standardized writing.

sources.title: Gwichin Tribal Council education
sources.note: Community education page on Elder teaching, experiential programs, language camps, science camps, and youth learning.

sources.title: Gwichin traditional knowledge
sources.note: Community research program on oral knowledge, plants, fish, animals, climate, place, and collaborative verification.

sources.title: Gwichin Ethnobotany
sources.note: Community publication page documenting foods, medicines, shelters, tools, named plants, Elders, and educational use.

sources.title: Gwichin Ethnobotany book
sources.note: Community book recording regionally specific plant knowledge, medicine preparation, tent materials, fuel, and named resources.

sources.title: Gwichin Social and Cultural Institute: Spruce
sources.note: Community plant record for spruce bough floors, fuel, shelter, insulation, smokehouses, caches, and medicinal steam.

sources.title: Gwichin traditional caribou skin clothing project
sources.note: Community-led reconstruction documenting caribou hide, sinew, quillwork, ochre, sewing labor, and regional artistic decisions.

sources.title: Gwichin material culture posters
sources.note: Community materials on dog packs, fish traps, willow-bark nets, caribou snares, and object-based knowledge.

sources.title: Gwichin Traditional Knowledge at a Crossroads
sources.note: Community research on Elders, children, family histories, land learning, knowledge transmission, and colonial disruption.

sources.title: Gwichin heritage provisions
sources.note: Community heritage framework recognizing archaeology, oral history, place names, objects, records, and Gwichin authority.

sources.title: Sahtu Renewable Resources Board: An Ancient Heritage
sources.note: Regional Indigenous institution on seasonal rounds, fishing, caribou, food preservation, gatherings, dialects, and distinct practices.

sources.title: Sahtu Renewable Resources Board: Dene Knowledge
sources.note: Regional account of adaptive oral knowledge, specialized vocabulary, lived experience, and learning across generations.

sources.title: Sahtu Renewable Resources Board: Caribou in the Sahtu
sources.note: Regional account of caribou movements, subsistence, hides, observation, and differences among caribou populations.

sources.title: Dehcho First Nations principles and values
sources.note: Community principles connecting land, animals, seasons, Elders, collective responsibilities, sharing, and future generations.

sources.title: Dehcho First Nations: Nahe Nahodhe
sources.note: Community learning project joining Elders and youth around hides, spruce, camps, plants, laws, and practical skills.

sources.title: Parks Canada: Nahanni culture and history
sources.note: Federal park account combining Dene oral history and archaeology, mobility, extended-family groups, gatherings, trade, and fishing.

sources.title: Bryan Gordon: People of Sunlight, People of Starlight
sources.note: University Press archaeology of 13,000 artifacts from 1,002 northern hunting camps and seasonal caribou technologies.

sources.title: NWT Mackenzie Valley archaeological impact assessment
sources.note: Territorial archaeology report on late-precontact sites, projectile points, scrapers, hide abraders, and bone and antler technology.

sources.title: Native copper provenance in the Arctic and Subarctic
sources.note: Peer-reviewed archaeological study distinguishing copper sources, regional exchange, technologies, and specific Dene associations.

sources.title: Parks Canada: Vuntut caribou fences
sources.note: Federal and community-linked record of northern caribou fences, hunting knowledge, archaeology, and Gwichin stewardship.

sources.title: Government of Yukon: A Race Against the Clock
sources.note: Territorial account of ice-patch hunting, preserved wood, sinew, feathers, ancient tools, First Nations partners, youth, and Elders.

sources.title: Parks Canada: Trochek National Historic Site
sources.note: Hän place with late-precontact archaeology, fish camps, plant harvesting, skin work, storage, stories, and place names.

sources.title: Parks Canada: Tsekwa National Historic Site
sources.note: Dane-zaa stewarded archaeology linking deep occupation, hunting evidence, oral histories, stories, songs, and identity.

sources.title: Prince of Wales Northern Heritage Centre education kits
sources.note: Territorial museum resources on Dene fishing, stone tools, archaeology, birch-bark canoes, stories, and land camps.

sources.title: Prince of Wales Northern Heritage Centre: Sharing Our Stories, Sahtu
sources.note: Community voices and museum objects documenting hides, babiche, tools, travel, dyeing, family use, and object histories.

sources.title: Government of Northwest Territories: Saoyu and Ehdacho
sources.note: Sahtugotine teaching, healing, spiritual places, oral traditions, ancestral responsibility, and cooperative stewardship.

sources.title: Parks Canada: Thaidene Nene relationship plan
sources.note: Current multi-nation stewardship plan showing overlapping relationships, distinct partners, water, land, hides, and family needs.
